headline: Computational frameworks now score missense, splicing and promoter variant effects
label: Variant Effect Prediction Frameworks
summary: Large experimental and foundation-model datasets now allow calibrated benchmarking of variant effect predictors across exons, promoters and proteomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational prioritization of genomic variants and sequence elements against calibrated scores or benchmarks. OpenSplice supplies an experimental dataset of over 590,000 variants across more than 600 human exons for evaluating splicing predictors. A tRNA synthetase study finds that active-site interface distance predicts pathogenicity but adds little beyond AlphaMissense and EVE, except among score-ambiguous variants. A colorectal cancer study uses Evo2 delta scores to prioritize promoter variants, validated against GWAS. PFES scores missense variants by enrichment of 103 protein features across 20 functional classes. GDIv2 refines gene-level damage ranking by correcting for coding sequence length and normalizing CADD scores per gene. The shared advance is evaluation against experimental or association-based benchmarks, such as OpenSplice and GWAS validation, rather than prediction alone.
